what_happened: Scene: layout 10, grey 4-slot (two-pair) toaster, bread in slot 2 (left pair, pair 0). Stage 0 was skipped: 148-240 the open gripper came down over the bread. While closing around it (close 249, width 0.03), it pushed the bread and the pair-0 carriage down to 0.32 (bread -1.0 cm, far below the 0.9 switch-on). It lifted the untoasted bread out of the slot at 257-330 (lift 0.186 m). The toaster was never on. It then carried the bread across the kitchen (380-700), drove to the dining counter, and at 748-797 lowered it onto the plate. It ended lying flat on the plate (tilt 86 deg from its upright in-slot pose, 'tipped' from 643, already tilting in the gripper), which is a normal way to put toast on a plate. It released at 797, 0.05 m from the plate centre, and the bread stayed on the plate (at_target 773-2000). So it did the stage-1 motion correctly, but with untoasted bread. Afterwards it drove back to the kitchen and worked at the TOASTER OVEN's door and knobs (1048-1620), never at the 4-slot toaster, until timeout.
causal_chain: went straight for the bread instead of the lever (232) -> pulled out the untoasted bread (257-330; lever only 0.32 as a side-effect) -> toaster never switched on with the bread in it, so the toaster_on latch can never be set -> delivered the bread to the plate (released 797, on the plate) -> stage 1 cannot count without toasting; then went to the toaster oven
self_recovery: none: after delivering, it went to the toaster oven, not the toaster. Even pressing the toaster lever then would not have helped, since the bread was no longer in the slot.
official_criterion_notes: The official conditions correctly refuse this episode: bread on the plate, gripper away, but never toasted. The packet's objects.obj.at_target_intervals [[773,2000]] could be misread as a delivered success; stage 1 never holds because toaster_on was never latched.
